items.title: 67460_Sammy Price oral history interview
items.q: This is where King Cole used to play.

ctx.x: But we got in Chicago and I went around every morning to the breakfast dance. You see, they had a breakfast dance. This is a thing they had every morning. They used to have those here. They called it a breakfast dance, it's just where they had a special show...say at four o'clock, the place closed at four or five o'clock. They'd have music and a dance

and all of the people...I guess it was one way that each club would have of increasing its business and, you know, people who wouldn't have an opportunity to go could go. So, they had breakfast dances every morning at one of the different clubs. And I never will forget, on Sunday night it was at the Club De-Lisa that would have...that's where Albert Ammons was playing, you know. And they had a big show and all that, and they'd have this big breakfast dance and hundreds of people, you know, come and try to get in,…

And I never will forget one morning, they had a breakfast dance at 49th and South Parkway.// Earl Hines came in with a party and I jumped up from my table and ran over to the piano and started playing "Deep Forest." That's his theme song. And the people thought I was crazy, you know. "Man, don't you see Earl Hines"? and "What are you trying to play his song...," you know. I only wanted to let Earl Hines know that I loved him so, that I knew his song. But the guys made it look like that I was crazy. So I had to…
